p.i: seruat à morte, & in bello à gladio. Prouer. 1o.cap. [?] Dominus animam iusti non sinit esurire. Quæ verba author noster pie & docte in Comment. suis expendit. Hæc gnome(in-quit) dulcissimam consolationem contra tentationem de victu continet. Vix autem maior est tentatio. Semper enim veremur, ne fame pereamus: & quanto morti sumus vi-ciniores, tanto magis hac cura tangimur. Augent in nobis hoc malum, peruersa mundi studia, & impia prouerbia, quæ circum-fert de parandis diuitiis per fas & nefas. Nisi vero repugnemus huic tentationi, ad impias vias conuertimur, quibus victum paremus, & in magna scelera ruimus, in furta, rapinas, latrocinia, sacrilegia, proditi-tiones: multi relinquunt uxores & liberos, atque in desperationem interdum incidunt. Hæc igitur sententia, & aliæ similes, dili-genter expendendæ sunt, vt contra pericu-losissimam tentationem, conscientias munimus. Et mox: Iustum vocat, qui fiduciam suam in Deo ponit, qui scit se ab eo seruari ac gubernari, suamq; vocationem sectatur,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "1o.cap." (the numeral may be "10"; marked [?]). The line break "esu / rire" has no printed hyphen, so it is written as "esurire". The mark after "tanto" is a small printed mark that I could not identify and left out. "circum-fert" is printed with a hyphen at the line end and is copied as printed. "Hæc gnome(in-quit)" has a hyphen at the line end. The text is set in italic throughout, so the whole paragraph is marked as italic. The paragraph continues onto the next page, so the page ends mid-sentence.
